newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Tuesday on a technical correction after Monday's rise, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell to 7.50 percent from 9.25 percent on Monday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market plunged to 1.2 million lots from 4.8 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the repo rates had a technical correction on Tuesday on a lack of fresh market-moving news after being pushed up on Monday due to a rise on the stock markets.

Another negative factor was a report on Tuesday by the Beijing-based Financial Times, which said China had stopped paying an anti-inflationary subsidy on long-term bank deposits due to falling inflation.
"The report further weakened market sentiment after falling inflation had already exerted downward pressure on the repo contracts," said one trader.
But the rising domestic A share markets supported the shortest three-day contract, which rose to 8.0 percent from Monday's 6.5 percent.
Traders said they believed the rates, especially the early- maturing rates, would rise in the next few days if the A share markets continued their strong run.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Tuesday due to their high yields but trading was dull with funds flowing to the active stock markets, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 111.35 yuan from 111.16 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell sharply to 511,984 lots from 1.04 million lots.
